title: Tree Grove
description: Traversals, recursion and binary search trees.

challenges.prompt: Tap the nodes in preorder: node, then left subtree, then right subtree.
challenges.explanation: Preorder visits a node before its children: A, then all of B's subtree (B, D, E), then C's (C, F, G).

challenges.prompt: Tap the nodes in postorder: left subtree, right subtree, then the node.
challenges.explanation: Postorder finishes both children before the parent, so the root comes last. It is the order you would use to delete a tree safely.

challenges.prompt: This is a binary search tree. Tap the nodes in inorder: left subtree, node, right subtree.
challenges.explanation: Inorder traversal of a BST always comes out sorted. That makes it a quick way to validate a BST or find the k-th smallest value.

challenges.prompt: You want to save a tree to a file and rebuild exactly the same shape later. Which traversal (with markers for empty children) is the usual choice?
challenges.explanation: Preorder writes each parent before its children, so when rebuilding you always create a node before you need to attach anything to it.

challenges.prompt: Compute the maximum depth of a binary tree recursively.
challenges.explanation: An empty tree has depth 0. Each node adds 1 to the deeper of its two subtrees; forgetting the + 1 always returns 0.

challenges.prompt: The max_depth function visits each node once. Time complexity for a tree with n nodes?
options: O(h²) where h is the height
challenges.explanation: Every node is visited exactly once, doing O(1) work: O(n). The call stack uses O(h) memory, where h is the height.

challenges.prompt: You insert 1, 2, 3, ..., n into a plain (non-balancing) BST in that order. How long does a search take now?
challenges.explanation: Sorted inserts make every node a right child, so the tree is really a linked list. Self-balancing trees (AVL, red-black) prevent this.

challenges.prompt: Find the lowest common ancestor of two values in a BST. What is the key idea?
options: Store every root-to-node path, then compare
Walk down from the root: go left if both values are smaller, right if both are larger, otherwise stop
challenges.explanation: The first node where the two values split to different sides (or where you hit one of them) is the LCA. O(h) time, O(1) extra space.
